latest_release.name: rig-v0.46.0
latest_release.body:
### Added

- *(rig-mcp-client)* new plugin crate `rig-mcp-client` (`rig_mcp_client::McpPlugin`), listed off in the default `plugins.toml`: MCP servers' tools (stdio and streamable HTTP) as `<server>__<tool>`, from `$RIG_HOME/mcp.json` and `<project>/.rig/mcp.json`. A project's server starts only once approved as written (`/mcp approve`, `/mcp deny`); `/mcp add` and `/mcp remove` edit the right file. `McpCorePlugin` and `AddMcpServer` let a front add its client's servers for one run. The `mcpServers` format with `type`, `disabled` and `${VAR}` expansion, with other fields refused by name for that server only, and `[mcp] connect_timeout_secs` (30). A sessionless run starts no `mcp.json` server. Headless `--tools` can name a tool a plugin registers in the background, such as `<server>__<tool>` (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2938](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2938), [#2948](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2948))
- *(rig-acp)* `rig acp`, an optional plugin: the coding agent for ACP v1 clients (Zed, Neovim plugins), with a rig process per session, rig's models, sign-in, tools, sessions and slash commands, permissions and forms, client MCP servers through rig-mcp-client, and history replayed from rig's own session (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2948](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2948))
- *(rig-claude-cloak)* an opt-in Linux and macOS plugin for Anthropic subscription OAuth and compatible request shaping under a separate `claude-cloak/*` provider, published with every release as `rig-claude-cloak` and listed disabled in the default `plugins.toml` (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2875](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2875), [#2891](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2891))
- *(rig-traffic)* new default plugin `rig_traffic::TrafficPlugin`: `--traffic-log`, or `[traffic] log = true` in `settings.toml`, records every model provider exchange in the session's `traffic.jsonl`, beside `effects.jsonl`. It runs on `rig-cassette`'s `traffic::TrafficLog` (feature `traffic`), which writes each exchange as one scrubbed, versioned JSON line (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2893](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2893))
- *(rig-basics)* `AgentsMdPlugin` puts the `AGENTS.md` files from the working directory up to the repository root, and `RIG_HOME/AGENTS.md`, in the system prompt. `SkillsPlugin` lists skills (`SKILL.md`, the Agent Skills format) from `.rig/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `RIG_HOME/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`, with `/skill:<name> [text]`. `/login <provider>` saves a provider's API key, used before its environment variable, and `/logout` removes it (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2873](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2873))
- *(sqlite, postgres)* `SqliteSessionStore` and `PostgresSessionStore` (feature `memory`): rig-memory sessions kept in a database shared by every process or worker. The facade's `memory` feature enables them with `sqlite` or `postgres`; `rig_memory::conformance::check_store` (feature `test-utils`) is the contract suite a store runs (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2890](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2890))
- *(memory)* `rig_memory::migration`: a chain of whole-session format steps the agent runs when it opens a session in an earlier format, keeping a copy of the session as it was. The shipped chain has no step. `rig_memory::summarized_in_log` reports what each compaction took out (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2899](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2899), [#2918](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2918))
- *(agent)* `AgentBuilder::provider_tool` and `provider_tools`: provider-hosted tools ride on every request the agent makes, after its function tools, and satisfy `ToolChoic

detail.readme: [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rig.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rig) [![docs.rs](https://img.shields.io/docsrs/rig)](https://docs.rs/rig) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/511303648119226382?label=Discord)](https://discord.gg/playgrounds) Rig is a Rust library for building applications on large language models. It also ships `rig`, a terminal coding agent built on the library that you extend with Bevy plugins. ## The coding agent ```bash cargo install rig rig ``` This installs the launcher. Until the next release it is 0.46.0, and [its guide](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/blob/v0.46.0/docs/agent.md) is on its tag. The [agent guide](docs/agent.md#install-and-run) describes `main` and how to install it from a checkout. The agent needs Rust 1.97.1 or newer and runs on Linux and macOS. The first `rig` builds the agent, which takes several minutes, and opens it. Run `/login` to sign in or save an API key, or export one such as `OPENAI_API_KEY` before starting. `/model` picks a model and `/help` lists the commands. `rig -p "fix the failing test"` answers one prompt and exits. Its tools, commands, sessions, sign-in and terminal view are each a plugin, so any of them can be turned off, replaced or added to. `/reload` rebuilds the agent with your changes and keeps the session. - The [agent guide](docs/agent.md) covers updating, models, sessions, tools, settings and scripting. - The [plugin guide](crates/rig-harness/PLUGINS.md) explains the basics of a plugin and points at working examples of each kind. ## The library ```bash cargo add rig anyhow cargo add tokio --features macros,rt-multi-thread ``` ```rust use rig::prelude::*; use rig::providers::openai::{self, OpenAI}; #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> { // Reads OPENAI_API_KEY. let model = OpenAI::from_env()?.completion(openai::GPT_6_2_SOL); let agent = AgentBuilder::new(model) .preamble("You are a comedian.") .build(); let response = agent.prompt("Entertain me!").await?; println!("{}", response.output()); Ok(()) } ``` Rig puts over 20 model providers and a dozen vector stores behind one interface. It has agents with tools, streaming and typed hooks. It covers completion, embedding, transcription, audio and image models and follows the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions. `rig-core` and `rig-agent` build for browser WASM. See [`examples/`](examples), the [guides](https://rig.rs/docs) and the [API reference](https://docs.rs/rig). ## Crates The `rig` crate re-exports `rig-core`. Its default features add `rig-agent`, the derive macros, the reqwest HTTP client with rustls and, on native targets, the `rig` launcher (feature `cli`, from `rig-cli`); `default-features = false` leaves them out. Each crate in the list below is a feature named after it without `rig-`: ```bash cargo add rig --features memory,fastembed ``` - Agents and state: [`rig-agent`](crates/rig-agent), [`rig-memory`](crates/rig-memory) (saved conversations), [`rig-cassette`](crates/rig-cassette) (record and replay), [`rig-rmcp`](crates/rig-rmcp) (MCP tools). - Models: [`rig-bedrock`](crates/rig-bedrock), [`rig-vertexai`](crates/rig-vertexai), [`rig-gemini-grpc`](crates/rig-gemini-grpc), [`rig-candle`](crates/rig-candle) (local models), [`rig-fastembed`](crates/rig-fastembed) (local embeddings), [`rig-typesafeai`](crates/rig-typesafeai) (TypeSafe Jev judgments). The vector stores, such as LanceDB, Qdrant and PostgreSQL, are companion crates behind features too; [docs.rs lists every feature](https://docs.rs/crate/rig/latest/features). Internals: [`rig-core`](crates/rig-core) (messages, models, tools, providers), [`rig-derive`](crates/rig-derive) (feature `derive`), [`rig-http`](crates/rig-http) (transport traits), [`rig-reqwest`](crates/rig-reqwest) (feature `reqwest`) and [`rig-tungstenite`](crates/rig-tungstenite) (feature `websocket`). Coding agent: [`rig-cli`](crates/rig-cli) (feature `cli`, the library of the `rig` binary) and, not facade features, [`rig-harness`](crates/rig-harness), [`rig-harness-protocol`](crates/rig-harness-protocol), [`rig-ecs`](crates/rig-ecs), [`rig-tools`](crates/rig-tools), [`rig-markdown`](crates/rig-markdown), and the plugins [`rig-basics`](plugins/rig-basics), [`rig-tui`](plugins/rig-tui), [`rig-fold`](plugins/rig-fold), [`rig-steel`](plugins/rig-steel), [`rig-mcp-client`](plugins/rig-mcp-client), [`rig-acp`](plugins/rig-acp), [`rig-inspect`](plugins/rig-inspect), [`rig-traffic`](plugins/rig-traffic) and [`rig-claude-cloak`](plugins/rig-claude-cloak). ## Community Ask questions on [Discord](https://discord.gg/playgrounds). [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) says how to contribute, and [awesome-rig](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/awesome-rig) lists projects built on Rig. Rig is pre-1.0, so releases break APIs. The [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and [migration notes](MIGRATING.md) say what changed. Rig is MIT licensed.
